#   - the four nofrils colourscheme files. They were read and they contain no
#     regular expressions at all: 130 hi lines, four if/exists guards and two
#     function bodies that call :hi, and not one pattern between them. There is
# Two things about the oracle itself, because they decide which rows can exist:
#   - vim answers through match() and matchstr() over a String, where a line
#     break is an ordinary character. In a buffer it is not: there, "." and the
#     negated classes stop at the end of a line and "^" and "$" anchor to one.
#     So rows whose input contains a line break are only here when both readings
#     give the same answer, which is the \_ forms, \n and the collections. The
#     line-break behaviour of "." and of the anchors is asserted directly in
#   - the script runs :s/x/bc/ before the first case, so "~" expands to "bc".
#     Compile the rows with Options{LastSubstitute: "bc"} and everything else
#     zero: 'ignorecase' and 'smartcase' are off and 'magic' is on, which is
#     what --clean gives and what the script sets explicitly anyway.
